programme: NOTCH1 sits at the centre of a corepressor-gated differentiation switch: NOTCH1 and NCOR1 both regulate HES1 (NCOR1/SMRT-type corepressors hold HES1 off at RBPJ sites until Notch intracellular domain displaces them — a documented general Notch mechanism), and NOTCH1 shares BCL2 with TRPS1, a GATA-family repressor that also controls VEGFA/PECAM1/ZEB2/RUNX2. Together these three read as a Notch-corepressor toggle that decides whether a progenitor/stem population differentiates (smooth muscle, endothelium, crypt epithelium) or stays proliferative/survival-primed (BCL2, HES1).
role_in_a: In cardiovascular disease, NOTCH1 is a load-bearing gene (Open Targets top-15th percentile of 260 CVD genes) governing arterial/venous identity, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and vascular smooth-muscle maturation (its target set here includes MYH11, GATA2/3, HEY2, CDH2, NFKB1/2) — the same axis mutated in bicuspid aortic valve and calcific aortic valve disease. NCOR1 and TRPS1 would be expected to act as brakes on this differentiation programme (repressing HES1/BCL2 and VEGFA/PECAM1 respectively) until Notch signal fires, shaping vascular remodeling and calcification.
role_in_b: In rectal cancer, Notch signalling sustains the crypt/cancer stem-cell state and drives EMT; NOTCH1 shows only moderate independent association here (62nd percentile of 2457 genes) but TRPS1 is strongly placed (7th percentile), consistent with its emerging role as an epithelial/stem-associated repressor. Loss of the NCOR1/TRPS1 brake on HES1, BCL2 and ZEB2 would be expected to favour stemness, survival and EMT in tumour epithelium.
shared_axis: The same Notch/corepressor toggle that decides progenitor-vs-differentiated fate in the vessel wall (smooth muscle/endothelial maturation) is redeployed at the intestinal crypt to decide stem-vs-differentiated epithelial fate; both diseases would represent a shift of that toggle toward the undifferentiated, survival-primed state (via HES1/BCL2) in their respective tissue.
reasoning: NOTCH1 and TRPS1 each carry an independent Open Targets association in one disease, and the NOTCH1–NCOR1 (HES1) and NOTCH1–TRPS1 (BCL2) links are shared targets within this dataset rather than invented, so the module is nameable and partly anchored. But no retrieved paper documents NCOR1 or this triad in either disease, and the specific claim that the two diseases share this exact corepressor toggle is my mechanistic extension, not something the record states — hence moderate rather than strong.
support: none found for NOTCH1, NCOR1, or TRPS1 directly in either disease from the retrieved literature (only Open Targets association scores place them); adjacent but not carrying-factor evidence exists elsewhere in this network — PMID 34876190 discusses ELF3 in colorectal (not rectal-specific) tumor microenvironment, and PMID 23745026 profiles CREB3L1 in rectal-cancer radiotherapy transcriptomes — neither addresses the NOTCH1/NCOR1/TRPS1 triad.
how_to_falsify: In matched vascular smooth-muscle/endothelial cells and rectal-tumor organoids, pharmacologically block Notch (γ-secretase inhibitor) or knock down NOTCH1, and check whether HES1 and BCL2 move concordantly with NCOR1/TRPS1 occupancy at those promoters (ChIP for NCOR1/TRPS1 before and after Notch blockade) in both tissues; if HES1/BCL2 regulation is Notch-independent in one tissue or NCOR1/TRPS1 do not occupy the same sites as RBPJ/NOTCH1, the shared-toggle account fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (CVD) vs colorectal (rectal cancer) — a cross-tissue comparison built from only 6 independent cohort pairs generating 160 patient-group comparisons, so the apparent breadth of concordance is smaller in independent-evidence terms than the raw count suggests. NOTCH1/NCOR1/TRPS1 are mid-recurrence factors (61-74/160), not the top-recurring ones (ELF4 at 86/160 has no supporting record at all and was deliberately excluded from the carrying set). The discordant POU2F2 and single-view factors (SIX1, ZMIZ1, IRF8, etc.) are excluded because they either disagreed between diseases or only led one patient subgroup. The tissue-generic exclusion list strips out the blood/immune backbone (STAT1/3, IRF1/4/8, CEBPB/D, NFATC2, RELB, SPIB, STAT5A, TFE3) — confirming that what remains is enriched for developmental/lineage regulators rather than a generic inflammatory signature, which supports reading this as a differentiation-switch story rather than an immune one, but also means the account rests on a narrow slice (3 of 11 concordant factors) of the full list.
